QF.id: Securities Types Features and Asset Allocation Concepts_13

question.text: A callable bond gives which party the right to redeem the bond before its original maturity date?

explanation.text: The Logic: Callable bonds allow the issuer to redeem the bonds prior to their original maturity date. Such bonds have a call option embedded in the bond contract that lets the issuer alter the terms. Issuers typically exercise this when interest rates fall -- they can retire expensive debt and reissue at lower rates. The Trap: If the investor has the right to seek early redemption, it is called a puttable bond (option B describes a put, not a call). Stock exchanges (option C) and rating agencies (option D) have no role in early redemption decisions.
